nodes.name: Definition 3.2
nodes.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a dihedral cone spherical surface. 
\begin{enumerate}
    \item Let $D$ be a developing map such that $\rho(\pi_1)\subset \mathrm{O}(2)$. 
    Then $\textcolor{black}{F}:=\pi_* D^*(\mathcal{F})$ and $\textcolor{black}{G}:=\pi_* D^*(\mathcal{G})$ are well-defined measured foliation s on $\Sigma$.
    $F$ and $G$ are also called \emph{latitude and longitude foliation} of $\Sigma$ with respect to $D$, regarded as horizontal and vertical foliation.
    
    \item 
    $\Sigma$ together with a pair of latitude and longitude foliation $(F,G)$ is called a \emph{foliated (dihedral) surface}, denoted by a triple \textcolor{black}{$(\Sigma;F,G)$}.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Definition 4.4
nodes.statement: Given a foliated surface $(\Sigma;F,G)$, the critical leaves $\mathrm{Crit}(G)$ partition the surface into a finite number of bigons. This partition is called the \emph{strip decomposition} of $(\Sigma;F,G)$.

nodes.name: Definition 5.4
Definition 4.18
nodes.statement:
A foliated surface $(\Sigma;F,G)$ is said to be \emph{generic} if each boundary of the bigons in strip decomposition contains exactly one marked point.
        This is equivalent to the absence of a singular leaf connecting zeroes of $G$.

nodes.name: Definition 4.16
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi\in[0,c)$. A \emph{$\psi$-longitude (right) twist deformation} of $(\Sigma;F,G)$ along $B$ is cutting $\Sigma$ along $\gamma$ and re-gluing $\gamma^+,\gamma^-$ by the identification
    \[ f_\gamma^+([x]_c) \sim f_\gamma^-([x+\psi]_c) \]
    for all $x\in [0,c]$. Here for any $t\in\mathbb{R}$, $[t]_c$ is the real number in $[0,c)$ such that $[t]_c \equiv t (\mathrm{mod}\ c)$.

nodes.name: Proposition 5.5
Corollary 4.20
nodes.statement: Non-generic foliated surfaces form a lower dimensional subset in $\mathcal{M}sphF_{g,n}^D(\vec{\theta};\vec{T})$ or $\mathcal{M}sphF_{g,n}^C(\vec{\theta};\vec{T})$ for every possible type partition $\vec{T}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.8
nodes.statement:
Let $\vec{\theta}:=(\theta_1, \cdots, \theta_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n_+$ be an angle vector with $\theta_i\neq1$ and $\vec{T}=( E, O, N )$ be a type partition with $ \#E=n_E, \#O=n_O, \#N=n_N $.
    If $\mathcal{M}sph_{g,n}^D(\vec{\theta};\vec{T})$ is non-empty, then its real dimension is 
    $$ 2n_E+n_O+2g-2. $$

nodes.name: Proposition 5.2
nodes.statement:
~\\
    For strict dihedral $(\Sigma;F,G)$, $\#\{ G_\Gamma/\mathrm{O}(2) \}$ is 1 or 3. And $\#\{ G_\Gamma/\mathrm{O}(2) \}=3$ if and only if $\Gamma$ is isomorphic to the Klein-4 group $K4:= \mathbb{Z}_2 \times \mathbb{Z}_2$.

    In other words, $\#\{p^{-1}(\Sigma)\} \leq 3$ for all $\Sigma\in\mathcal{M}sph^D_{g,n}(\vec{\theta})$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5.10
nodes.statement:
Let $\vec{\theta}:=(\theta_1, \cdots, \theta_n) \in \mathbb{R}^n_+$ be an angle vector with $\theta_i\neq1$, and let $\vec{T}_0$ be the maximal type partition as above. 
    Then whenever the moduli space is non-empty, the maximal dimension of $\mathcal{M}sph^D_{g,n}(\vec{\theta})$ is
    
    
    
    
    
    \[ 2M_E+M_O+2g-2. \]
